narrative:
The model estimates an 83% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outlook, in order of importance, were your total years of professional experience, whether you had received other job offers, and how long you have been with this current organization.

Your 6–10 years of overall experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter experience (50% have only 1–5 years), the model sees mid-level experience like yours as often signaling readiness to move on to new opportunities. Similarly, the fact that you have received other job offers strongly increased the likelihood of departure, as external opportunities are a common reason people ultimately decide to leave. Finally, your 1–5 years in this specific role also contributed to the prediction of leaving. Most employees the model expects to stay have either very short or much longer tenure here, so this intermediate period appears to be a transitional window.

Taken together, these elements suggest the organization sees you as someone with growing options and enough background to act on them. You and your manager should discuss what would increase your sense of long-term fit and stability here, whether through clearer advancement paths, better recognition of your experience, or addressing any external pulls you may be feeling. Understanding these drivers can help turn the outlook around. (248 words)
